subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: 'Polyphonic' (or contrapuntal) texture means:
options: Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together
questions.explain: Polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic lines.

questions.q: Repeating a short melodic pattern at higher or lower pitches in turn is called a:
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic idea at successively higher or lower pitches.

questions.q: The harmonic minor scale differs from the natural minor by raising which note?
questions.explain: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh note by a semitone, creating a leading note.

questions.q: What does a natural sign do?
options: Cancels a previous sharp or flat
Lowers a note by a tone
Raises a note by a tone
questions.explain: A natural cancels a sharp or flat, returning the note to its natural pitch.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'staccato' tells a player to make notes:
questions.explain: Staccato means short and detached, the opposite of legato.

questions.q: Compared with a major scale, a (natural) minor key generally sounds:
questions.explain: Minor keys typically sound darker or sadder than the brighter major.

questions.q: Which note value lasts the longest?
questions.explain: A semibreve lasts four beats in 4/4, longer than a minim, crotchet or quaver.

questions.q: Which time signature is an example of compound time?
questions.explain: 6/8 is compound time because each beat divides into three quavers (two dotted-crotchet beats).

questions.q: The articulation marking 'accent' (>) tells a performer to:
options: Hold the note longer than written
questions.explain: An accent mark instructs the player to stress or emphasise that note.

questions.q: What does a 'crescendo' instruct a performer to do?
questions.explain: A crescendo is a gradual increase in volume, opposite to a diminuendo.

questions.q: Which term describes a melody supported by chords moving in the same rhythm?
questions.explain: Homophonic texture is a clear melody accompanied by chords.

questions.q: The interval from C up to G is a:
questions.explain: C up to G spans five letter names, making a perfect 5th.

questions.q: What does 'rit.' (ritardando) mean?
questions.explain: Ritardando means to gradually slow the tempo down.

questions.q: A chromatic scale moves entirely in:
questions.explain: A chromatic scale ascends or descends entirely in semitones, using all twelve pitches.

questions.q: How many beats does a dotted minim last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A dot adds half the note's value, so a minim (2 beats) plus its dot (1 beat) lasts three beats.

questions.q: Using repetition when developing a musical idea helps to:
options: Make ideas memorable and give a sense of unity
questions.explain: Repetition makes musical ideas memorable and gives a piece unity and coherence.

questions.q: 'Quantising' in a DAW is used to:
options: Correct the timing of notes onto the beat
questions.explain: Quantising snaps recorded notes to the nearest beat to tidy up their timing.

questions.q: What does a single dot placed after a note do to its value?
options: Adds half the note's value again
questions.explain: A dot after a note increases its length by half of its original value.

questions.q: On a string instrument, the technique 'pizzicato' means to:
options: Pluck the strings with the finger
questions.explain: Pizzicato instructs the player to pluck the strings rather than bow them.

questions.q: A minor triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A minor triad stacks a minor 3rd then a major 3rd, giving its darker sound.

questions.q: Which cadence creates a surprise by moving from chord V to chord VI instead of I?
questions.explain: An interrupted cadence moves from V to VI, surprising the listener who expects a perfect cadence.

questions.q: In music technology, 'panning' a sound controls:
options: Its position between the left and right speakers
questions.explain: Panning places a sound in the stereo field, between the left and right speakers.
